execution_envelope.distinction: The 600-second bounded execution turn is not the 900-second P0 acceptance window. P0 windows are fixed epoch-anchored wall-clock windows and may span multiple bounded turns.

active_retest.purpose: Second bounded-turn retest plus first predictive-prearm canary.

fixed_window_context.reason: The worker was first observed 106 seconds after the fixed window opened; unknown time cannot be inferred as useful.

latest_diagnosis.evidence: P0 requires 840/900 = 93.33% useful coverage. A steady 600s useful-turn + 60s post-close gap has an idealized ceiling of 90.91% before scheduler/startup overhead; a prior production sample observed about 64s scheduler delay after due.
latest_diagnosis.implication: The verified completion-relative fallback cannot reliably satisfy P0 as the optimized normal path. Scheduler latency must be reduced, hidden under predecessor useful work, or replaced by a faster independent wake adapter.

next_corrective_experiment.hypothesis: Predictively arming the same-canonical successor before predecessor close can hide scheduler delivery latency under still-useful predecessor work while preserving single substantive authority and the 780s cold-rescue safety model.
next_corrective_experiment.candidate_change: First canary armed 30s before target close. Early successor fences/observes only while predecessor is fresh/conflicting.
next_corrective_experiment.success_signal: Two safe same-canonical predictive-prearm handoffs with observed post-close useful-work gap <=42s and no duplicate substantive side effect/schedule rollback, followed by a valid fixed 900s window.
